FOREWORD

0.1 This Indian Standard (First Revision) was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 31 August 1971, after the draft finalized by the Oils and Oilseeds Sectional Committee had been approved by the Chemical Division Council and the Agricultural and Food Products Division Council. 0.2 Stearic acid is used in the manufacture of various products, such as rubber, textile auxiliaries, cosmetics, metallic stearates, and plastics and leather goods. Taking into consideration the requirements of the different grades of the material being manufactured and used in the country, this standard was originally issued in 1960. In this revision, the grades have deen renamed as types and the requirements for Types 4 and 5 which are used in the rubber industry have been modified, in particular the limits of saponification value, acid value, copper and ash. 0.3 The technical grades of stearic acid are manufactured to contain varying amounts of palmitic acid. It is for this reason that different types have different characteristics in respect of saponification value, iodine value and titre. 0.4 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS: 2� 1960*0 The number of aignificant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

1. SCOPE
1.1 This standard prescribes the requirements and the methods of sampling and test for stearic acid, technical.
�Rules (or rounding off numerical values ( reoised],

It shall be glossy and the material conforming to Type I shall he crystalline to the naked eve. When melted, it shall form .1 clear and transparent liquid

PACKING

~.I

The material shall be supplied in suitable containers as agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier.

5. MARKING
5.1 The containers shall be securely dosed and legibly and indelibly marked with the following information: a) b) c) d) e) f) Manufacturer's name; Recognized trade-mark, if any; Name and type of the material; Mass of the material in the container; Month. and year of manufacture; and Batch number in code or otherwise to enable the lot of manufacture to be traced from records.

5.1.1 The containers may also be marked with Standard Mark.
5J.1 The use of tbe Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of tbe Bureau of Indian Standards Act. 1986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The details of conditions under whicb tbe licence for the usc of Standard Mark may be gnnted to manufacturers or producers may be obtained from the Bureau of Indian Standards.

6. SAMPLING
6.1 Representative samples of the material -nall he drawn as pI escribe d in Appendix B.

7. TESTS
7.1 Tests shall be carried out hy ,11<- methods prescribed in IS ~ :)411-1%4� and in Appendix A.

APPENDIX A ( Table 1, ann Clause 7.1 )
TESTS FOR MINDAL ACIDITY, ASH, HEAVY METALS AND COPPER A-I. Q.UALITY OF REAGENTS

A-t.t Unless specified otherwise, pure chemicals and distilled water (set
IS: 1070-1960� ) shall be employed in tests.
NOTa - 'Pure chemicals' shall mean chemicals that do not contain impurities which affect the results of analysis.

A-2. TEST FOR MINERAL ACIDITY

A-l.t Reagent. A-2.1.1 Petroleum Ether - 60/80�C grade.
A-2.1.Z Methyl Orange Indicator - 0'05 percent (m/D) solution.

A-Z.l Procedure - Measure 10 ml of the melted sample into a separating funnel and shake intimately with three successive lO-ml portions of hot water. The temperature of the hot water should be more than the melting point of stearic acid. Combine the aqueous extracts, transfer to another separating funnel and remove traces of fatty acids in the water by extraction with petroleum ether. Test the aqueous extract with a few drops of methyl orange indicator.
A-2.2.1 The material shall be taken to have passed the test if the indicator does not show acid reaction.
A-3. DETERMINATION OF ASH A-3.t Apparatu. A-3.1.1 Platinum Crucible ( or Silica lJish ) A-3.t.:Z Desiccator calcium chloride.
containing an efficient desiccant, such as fused

A-3.2 Procedure - Weigh accurately about 10 g of the material into a platinum crucible ( or silica dish) which has been previously ignited, cooled in the desiccator and weighed. Dry the material in the crucible at 90 � 2�C for 2 hours. Then heat over a low flame and ignite the contents gently. Incinerate the residue in a muffle furnace at 3:>U � 10 e until
0

free from carbon. Cool the crucible in a desiccator and weigh, Repeat th(' above procedure of heating, cooling and wt'ighm~ until thl" difference between two successive w("ighing~ does not exceed I mg. Preserve the ash for test in A-4.

A,-4. TEST FOR HEAVY METALS .-4.1 Apparatus A-4.1.1 Nessler Cylinders - 50 ml capacity. A-4.2 Reagent. A-4.2.1 Concentrated Hydrochloric Acid - conforming to IS : 265�1962�. A-4.2.2 Conan/rated Nitric Acid - conforming to IS: 264-196R t . A-4.2.3 Acetic Acid I N.

A-4.2.4 Ammonium Chloride A-4.2.5 Standard Lead Solution - Dissolve 1'600 !; of lead nitrate in water, add I ml of concentrated nitric acid (conforming to IS : 2M-1968t) and make up the volume to 1000 rnl. Pipette out 10 ml of the solution and dilute again to 1000 ml with water. One millilitre of solution contains 0'01 mg of lead (as Pb).
A.4.2.6 Hydrogen Sulphid� Solution freshly prepared saturated solution.

A�4.3 Procedure - Extract the ash, as obtained in A-3.2, with 1 ml of concentrated hydrochloric acid and transfer to an evaporating dish after washing a number of times with water. Add 0'5 ml of concentrated nitric acid and evaporate to dryness over a steam-bath. Dissolve the residue in 20 ml of water and 8 ml of acetic acid, and dilute to 250 rnl with water. Mix well and filter. Transfer 25 ml of the filtrate to the Nessler cylinder and add I g of ammonium chloride in it. Carry out a control test in an other Nessler cylinder using 2'0 ml of standard lead solution in place of
-Specification for hydrochloric acid ("viJtd), fSpecificadon for nitric acid (fi,st "visio/l).

,

IS I 1675 -1971
tlte material and I g uf ammonium chloride and I ml of acetic acid. To each Nessler cylinder add 10 ml of hydrogen sulphide solution dilute to the mark and shake well. Compare the intensity of colour produced in the two cylinders.

A-4.3.1 The limit prescribed in Table I shall be taken as not having been exceeded if the intensity of the colour obtained with the material is not greater than that obtained in the control test.
A-S. TEST FOR COPPER A-S.l Apparatu8 A-S.LI Nessler Cylinders -- 50 ml capacity. A-S.:: Reagents
A-S.l.I Dilute Hydrochloric Acid approximately 0'5 N.

A-S.2.l Citric Acid Solution - approximately 10 percent.
A-5.Z.J Ammonium Hydroxide - approximately I : 4 ( V/o).
A-5.~.4 Sodium Diethyldithiocarbamate Solution - Dissolve 0'1 g of sodium diethyldirhiocarbarnate in 100 ml of copper-free water. Filter, if necessary. Preserve in an amber-colour glass bottle and store in a dar k place. This solution should not be used after two weeks.

A-S.l.S Extraction Solvent - Two alternative extraction solvents, amyl alcohol and carbon tetrachloride, are prescribed. It is permitted to use any one of them.
A-S.l.6 Standard Copper Solution - Dissolve 0'392 8 ~ of copper sulphate pentahydrate (CuSO,.5H 20 ) in I 000 ml of copper-free water. Pipette out 10 ml of this solution and dilute to I 000 ml. One millilitre of the diluted solution contains 0'001 mg of copper (as Cu). The diluted solution should be freshly prepared before use.
NOTS -

The puritv of the salt should be checked before use.

A-S.3 Procedure - Take about 10'000 g of the material of Type I or
1'000 g of the material of Types 4 and 5, melt it and extract with hot dilute hydrochloric acid three or four times. Evaporate the acid. Cool and add 2'5 ml of citric acid solution. Neutralize the acidity with ammonium hydroxide and add 10 ml in excess, followed by 10 rnl of sodium diethyIdithiocarbamate solution. Transfer the solution to a separating funnel, stir and allow to stand for 5 minutes. Extract the yellow colour produced with 10 ml of the extraction solvent and collect the extractant in a Nessler cylinder and dilute to the mark. Carry out a control test using 10 ml or 8

IS � 1675� 1971
standard copper solution, proceeding exactly all for the material under test and collect the extractant in another Nessler cylinder. Compare the intensity of the colour produced in the two cylinders. A-5.3.1- The limit. laid down in Table I shall be taken as not having been exceeded if the intensity of colour produced with the material is not greater than that produced in the control test.

APPENDIX B ( Clause 6.1 )
SAMPLING OF STEARIC ACID, TECHNICAL B-1. GENERAL REQ,UIREMENTS OF SAMPUNG
8-1.0' In drawing, preparing, storing and handling test samples, followiog precautions and directions shall be observed.

'1-1.1 Samples shall not be taken in an exposed place.
11-1.2 The sampling instrument shall he clean and dry.

8-1.3 Precautions shall be taken to protect the samples, the material being
sampled, the sampling instrument and the containers for samples from adventitious contamination. B-I.4 To draw a representative sample, the contents of each container selected for sampling shall be mixed as thoroughly as possible by suitable means. 8-1.5 The samples shall be placed in clean, dry glass stoppered bottles.

8-1.6 The sample containers shall be of such a size that they are almost completely filled by the sample.
B-l.7 Each sample container shall be sealed air-tight after filling and marked with full details of sampling, the date of sampling and the year and month of manufacture of the material.

8-1.8 Samples shall be stored in such a manner that the temperature of
the material does not vary unduly from the normal temperature. B�2. SCALE OF SAMPLING B-2.0 Samples to determine conformity of the material to this specification shall be selected in accordance with the procedure given below. However, the purchaser and the supplier may agree to adopt any other procedure.

8--3.3 All the individual samples representing the selected containers and the composite sample representing the lot shall be divided into three equal parts, thus forming three sets of test samples. 8-3.4 Referee Sample - The third set of the test samples, bearing the <cals of the purchaser and the supplier shall constitute the referee sample and shall be used in case of dispute between the purchaser and the supplier. It shall be kept at a place agreed to between them. 8-4. NUMBER OF TESTS 8-4.1 The tests for saponification value, acid value and titre (see Table.l )
